name: Restatement (Second) of Torts — Invasion of Privacy
summary: The Restatement identifies four privacy torts recognized at common law, including intrusion upon seclusion and public disclosure of private facts, which courts use as benchmarks for determining whether modern statutory privacy claims constitute concrete injuries.
significance: Both parties cite common law privacy torts to argue whether the VPPA violation is sufficiently analogous to a historically recognized harm — the test established in TransUnion — with Salazar arguing it matches intrusion upon seclusion and Paramount arguing it does not match public disclosure torts.
